<div>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><a name="Parti_155942"></a><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">PART&nbsp;I</font></b></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 47.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-47.0pt;"><a name="Item1_Business_155943"></a><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">ITEM 1. Business</font></b></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><a name="General_155943"></a><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">General</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Dendrite International,&nbsp;Inc. (collectively, with
its subsidiaries, the &#147;Company,&#148; &#147;Dendrite,&#148; &#147;we,&#148; and &#147;our&#148;) was incorporated
in 1987 with a mission to improve sales and marketing productivity for
pharmaceutical and other life sciences companies. Dendrite pioneered and
quickly became the standard for pharmaceutical sales force automation, enabling
transparency between the home office and its sales force&#151;a relationship that
was formerly detached and paper-based.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Dendrite leverages its extensive knowledge of the
pharmaceutical industry&#146;s complex and unique selling process to deliver leading
and adaptive solutions. Our solutions are deployed in each of the world&#146;s top
20 pharmaceutical companies, in hundreds of large, mid-tier, and emerging
manufacturers, and in 59 countries around the globe. Every year hundreds of
millions of interactions are made using Dendrite&#146;s sales, marketing, clinical
and compliance solutions that are closely aligned with the growing needs of the
pharmaceutical industry</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In the mid 1990s, with the advent of prescriber volume
data, the pharmaceutical industry underwent a significant shift in the way it
went to market, aligning its efforts toward scaling sales forces to maximize
the number of contacts made with the highest volume prescribers. Dendrite led
the way with innovative functionality to support more complex sales
organization structures and integrated field support solutions to improve
productivity among the growing sales force</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Over the past few years, a
new evolutionary shift has taken shape as only a handful of pharmaceutical
companies have the sales force sizes to saturate the doctor&#146;s office, and
prescribers have become overwhelmed by sales visits. This trend, coupled with
the decreasing pipeline of new blockbuster drugs to carry growth, has led the
pharmaceutical industry to seek innovative solutions to drive market share. The
industry is moving away from a mono-focal dependence on sales representatives
toward a more integrated sales and marketing approach that allows it to reach
the right prescribers at the right time with the right message through the
right channel. As the complexity of selling, marketing, complying with
regulations and supporting clinical trials continues to increase, Dendrite has
continued to evolve and expand itself to cater to the industry&#146;s emerging
needs.</font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><a name="DendriteSolutions_155947"></a><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Dendrite Solutions</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Dendrite helps
pharmaceutical companies communicate effectively and efficiently with
prescribers to provide the information and knowledge that will help doctors
select the best available medication to improve their patients&#146; health. Our
solutions are grouped into four categories: Sales Solutions, Marketing
Solutions, Compliance Solutions, and Clinical Solutions.</font></p>


 <p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:24.0pt 0pt .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font face="Times New Roman">3</font></p> <br><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="center">

<!-- SEQ.=1,FOLIO='3',FILE='C:\fc\7416578630_D10565_927050\2977-1-ca.htm',USER='jmsproofassembler',CD='Mar 15 16:57 2006' -->
<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">


<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><a name="I_SalesSolutions_155947"></a><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">I. Sales Solutions</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In an
environment where time with the prescriber is decreasing and competition is
increasing, field sales representatives need state-of-the-art tools and
information that allow them to achieve their ultimate objective of delivering
timely and pertinent information to their customers&#151;the prescriber. Our suite
of Sales Solutions includes a comprehensive field and home based software suite
designed to enable pharmaceutical and life sciences companies to manage sales
force activities. The full suite of software and services in this category
includes:</font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><a name="I_SalesForceEffectivenesssfeSoftw_160032"></a><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">i. Sales
Force Effectiveness (SFE) Software</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">A comprehensive,
field-based product suite that helps pharmaceutical companies manage sales
force activities and includes both software licensing and maintenance.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><b><font style="font-weight:bold;">Mobile Intelligence</font></b><b><font face="Symbol" style="font-weight:bold;">&#212;</font></b>.
(Version 4.0). This is the next generation successor to WebForce<font face="Symbol">&#212;</font>,
Dendrite&#146;s flagship Sales Force Effectiveness (SFE) solution used to provide
visibility and direction between the pharmaceutical home office and the field
sales representative. As sales force automation solutions became more complex
over the years, there grew a need for a solution that not only provided better
functionality, but also allowed for better use by the sales representative.
Mobile Intelligence was developed using human centered design principles to
improve product usability via a more intuitive user interface that maps
directly to the daily workflow of sales representatives. The solution improves
field sales productivity as it promotes more efficient and effective detailing
interactions with customers and is available as an enterprise or On-Demand,
hosted version. Mobile Intelligence is built on a Microsoft .NET framework that
includes TIBCO Enterprise Application Integration (EAI) technologies. The
platform enables an open, extensible and configurable solution that is easily
integrated into a sales and marketing system environment.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 50.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><b><font style="font-weight:bold;">WebForceMedSurg</font></b><b><font face="Symbol" style="font-weight:bold;">&#212;</font></b><b><font style="font-weight:bold;">. </font></b>An SFE tool used to manage the specialized needs of
medical device and surgical sales forces.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 50.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><b><font style="font-weight:bold;">WebForceCG</font></b><b><font face="Symbol" style="font-weight:bold;">&#212;</font></b><b><font style="font-weight:bold;">. </font></b>An SFE tool used to manage the specialized needs of
consumer goods sales forces globally.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 50.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><b><font style="font-weight:bold;">j-force</font></b><b><font face="Symbol" style="font-weight:bold;">&#212;</font></b><b><font style="font-weight:bold;">. </font></b>A suite of
SFE tools specifically developed for the Asian hospital-driven
pharmaceutical market.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 50.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><b><font style="font-weight:bold;">J-centreSYNERGY</font></b><b><font face="Symbol" style="font-weight:bold;">&#212;</font></b><b><font style="font-weight:bold;">. </font></b>A solution that enables information exchange between
pharmaceutical companies and wholesalers.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 50.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><b><font style="font-weight:bold;">VisiForce</font></b><b><font face="Symbol" style="font-weight:bold;">&#212;</font></b><b><font style="font-weight:bold;">. </font></b>An SFE tool specifically for life science and
pharmaceutical companies in emerging international markets where organizing,
targeting, and evaluating potential prescribers is essential for the commercial
success of sales forces.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><b><font style="font-weight:bold;">Application Integration Server (AIS). </font></b>The AIS is the
integration hub for Dendrite&#146;s entire technology solution suite. It is a
cost-effective, flexible, and practical architecture that provides pre-built
integration between Dendrite products and allows Dendrite customers to
integrate Dendrite solutions within their own environment. AIS enables
customers to make better and more informed decisions in an environment where
data and activity must be shared and accessed at an individual prescriber level.
The AIS uses universal integration technologies (XML, Web Services), which
promotes the reuse of existing sales and marketing infrastructure investments
and standards.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><b><font style="font-weight:bold;">Analyzer</font></b><b><font face="Symbol" style="font-weight:bold;">&#212;</font></b><b><font style="font-weight:bold;">. </font></b>A flexible, easy-to-use data analysis tool that
standardizes the decision support and reporting processes for all levels of a
pharmaceutical sales organization. Analyzer is available as a .NET based as
well as a non-.NET based solution.</p>


 <p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:24.0pt 0pt .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font face="Times New Roman">4</font></p> <br><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="center">

<!-- SEQ.=1,FOLIO='4',FILE='C:\fc\7416578630_D10565_927050\2977-1-ca.htm',USER='jmsproofassembler',CD='Mar 15 16:57 2006' -->
<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">


<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><b><font style="font-weight:bold;">Organization Manager</font>&#174;. </b>A
comprehensive sales force resource management solution that was developed to
minimize interruption to the sales process, as pharmaceutical companies rapidly
redeploy and reorganize their sales force. The solution manages complex field
sales alignments linking sales representatives and managers to customers, geographies,
products, territories, and teams in order to promote an efficient and
productive sales environment.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><b><font style="font-weight:bold;">ForcePharma Geo</font></b><b><font face="Symbol" style="font-weight:bold;">&#212;</font></b>.
A geographical-based business intelligence tool used to share objectives or
sales results between the home office and the sales force. It provides the
sales force with an easy and intuitive way to analyze performance indicators
against the strategy set by the home office.</p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><a name="Ii_CustomerAnalytics_160102"></a><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">ii. Customer Analytics</font></b></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><b><font style="font-weight:bold;">360</font></b><b><font style="font-weight:bold;">&#176;</font> Insights</b><b><font face="Symbol" style="font-weight:bold;">&#212;</font>.</b>
As the pharmaceutical industry continues to experience pricing, regulatory and
pipeline pressures, sales and marketing integration has become paramount to
improving bottom line results. Dendrite&#146;s 360&#176; Insights enables sales and
marketing integration by providing transparency into brand, market, and sales
performance in one software application. This transparency enables integration
and collaboration between the sales and marketing organizations to gain
comprehensive, accurate, and actionable insights about their customers and
their brands that will support and grow their business by making adaptations to
sales and marketing tactical plans based on measured market responses.</p>

critical business decisions. Creating this &#147;single view of the customer&#148; enables the pharmaceutical company to
leverage up-to-date information for improved relationship marketing and
achieve more efficient selling.</p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Pharmaceutical

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><b><font style="font-weight:bold;">Integrated Support Center. </font></b>Support services that enhance the

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">With increased industry
pressure for brand performance as a result of fewer blockbuster drugs and
shorter patent expiries, the pharmaceutical industry has sought more efficient
ways to reach its prospects versus traditional mass-marketing techniques. Increasingly,
the pharmaceutical marketer is striving to reach prescribers based on
individualized adoption and prescribing behavior. Dendrite&#146;s Marketing
Solutions include powerful targeting tools, unique execution channels and the

prescribers at the right time, through the right channel with the right
message.</font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">i. <a name="I_TrgetingSolutions_160148"></a>Targeting Solutions</font></b></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><b><font style="font-weight:bold;">ScripMax</font></b><b><font face="Symbol" style="font-weight:bold;">&#212;</font>. </b>United States
business intelligence solutions that access anonymous longitudinal patient data
(LPD) to identify individual doctor prescribing changes. ScripMax was developed
for use in marketing campaigns to provide more precise targeting versus
traditional volume-based solutions. It enables the brand to more quickly
identify prescriber brand switching behavior and behavioral tendencies which
can be used to craft highly targeted, personalized proactive messages.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><b><font style="font-weight:bold;">Physician Connect</font></b><b><font size="1" style="font-size:6.5pt;font-weight:bold;position:relative;top:-3.0pt;">SM</font>.
</b>Dendrite&#146;s Physician Connect solution enables brand teams to identify
prescribers that influence peer script writing behavior. Unlike traditional key
opinion leader solutions, Physician Connect identifies local and regional
influencers within social or professional networks of trust. By targeting these
influencers with specific marketing and sales messaging, the rapid adoption of
a new product by these leaders catalyzes its adoption in localized markets.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><b><font style="font-weight:bold;">Practitioner Validation and Cleansing Services. </font></b>This

activity.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><b><font style="font-weight:bold;">Optas</font></b><b><font size="1" style="font-size:6.5pt;font-weight:bold;position:relative;top:-3.0pt;">TM</font>&#160;Database. </b>The Optas Database, used

captures and centralizes patient records acquired through various customer

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><b><font style="font-weight:bold;">Pharbase</font></b><b><font size="1" style="font-size:6.5pt;font-weight:bold;position:relative;top:-3.0pt;">TM</font>.

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><b><font style="font-weight:bold;">Docscan&#174;. </font></b>A

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><a name="Iii_ComplianceSolutions_160237"></a><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">III. Compliance Solutions</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">A solution suite powered
by Dendrite&#146;s BuzzeoPDMA division. These solutions unite market-leading

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><a name="I_SamplingSolutions_160240"></a><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">i. Sampling Solutions</font></b></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><b><font style="font-weight:bold;">Sample Guardian</font></b><b><font face="Symbol" style="font-weight:bold;">&#212;</font></b><b><font style="font-weight:bold;">. </font></b>A complete sample management tool used to track, analyze and

companies to comply with government regulations, specifically in the United

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><b><font style="font-weight:bold;">FDA/PDMA Consulting</font>. </b>A

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><b><font style="font-weight:bold;">Intelligent Allocations. </font></b>A comprehensive solution, combining

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><b><font style="font-weight:bold;">Reconciliation Services. </font></b>Services designed to enable

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><a name="Ii_FederalAndStateRegulatoryCompl_160247"></a><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">ii. Federal
and State Regulatory Compliance Solutions</font></b></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><b><font style="font-weight:bold;">Regulatory Consulting Services. </font></b>Services in this suite
include compliance auditing and gap analysis, mock inspections, standard
operating procedure development, program design and implementation, ongoing
support and guidance, staff augmentation, and liaising with federal and state
agencies. Consultation is provided to pharmaceutical and other life science
customers in the regulated areas of controlled substances, prescription drugs,
list I chemicals, and medical devices.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><b><font style="font-weight:bold;">Regulatory and Compliance Training Services. </font></b>Complete
regulation and compliance-specific training and collaborative educational
solutions delivered through traditional, web-based or blended training methods.
Dendrite develops and delivers training-program content, tailored to
specific requirements.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><b><font style="font-weight:bold;">State Services. </font></b>Dendrite provides guidance to companies to
assist them with understanding state regulatory requirements and registration
processes related to research, manufacturing, and the distribution of
pharmaceutical products, controlled substances, over-the-counter products, and
medical devices. Services are designed to provide assistance in licensing,
corporate changes, surveys, state license monitoring, state legislation and
regulation monitoring, Medicaid program, and Puerto Rico regulations.</p>


 <p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:24.0pt 0pt .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font face="Times New Roman">8</font></p> <br><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="center">

<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">


<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><b><font style="font-weight:bold;">Document Scanning and Data Capture. </font></b>An optical scanning,
imaging, character-recognition, and retrieval system designed for
efficient, economical sample accountability to assist our customers with their
regulatory compliance requirements.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><b><font style="font-weight:bold;">Computer Systems Auditing, Validation Services and Information
Technology Security. </font></b>Services focused on ensuring that our clients&#146;
software applications and systems meet business and regulatory requirements.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font style="font-weight:bold;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Note:</font></b></font><font face="Times New Roman" style="font-weight:normal;"> </font><font style="font-weight:normal;">In
2005, the Company&#146;s Compliance Solutions were marketed under the First Source
Sample and First Source Compliance Solutions brand categories.</font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><a name="Iv_ClinicalSolutions_160312"></a><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">IV. Clinical Solutions</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Dendrite offers a
set of solutions designed to benefit the clinical trial process by assisting in
effectively initiating studies, identifying potential investigators and
patients, providing ongoing support and training to investigators, conducting
pre- and post-marketing risk assessments, facilitating safety reporting, and
providing data analysis of trial and competitive drugs. Services include:</font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><b><font style="font-weight:bold;">Clinical Trial Accelerator Services</font></b><b><font size="1" style="font-size:6.5pt;font-weight:bold;position:relative;top:-3.0pt;">SM</font>. </b>Allow
pharmaceutical and other life sciences companies to expedite the initiation of
clinical trials, including protocol feasibility testing, eligible patient
population profiling, and investigator identification/qualification.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><b><font style="font-weight:bold;">Clinical Trial Effectiveness Solutions</font></b><b><font face="Symbol" style="font-weight:bold;">&#212;</font>.
</b>Designed to ensure two critical success factors for trials utilizing
clinical trial technologies:&#160; 1) trial
site productive up-time, and 2) trial site satisfaction. These success factors
are achieved through Dendrite&#146;s site assessment services, provisioning
services, connectivity services, application and data hosting services, site
training and site support.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font style="font-weight:bold;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Proactive Risk Management</font></b></font><b><font size="1" style="font-size:6.5pt;font-weight:bold;position:relative;top:-3.0pt;">SM</font></b><font style="font-weight:bold;"><b>.</b></font><b><font style="font-weight:bold;">&nbsp;&nbsp; </font></b>An intelligence-based service aimed
at delivering actual drug usage data and analysis through observational studies
and safety tracking tools that can be used to identify and analyze risk
situations before they adversely affect the product life cycle.</p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><a name="Customers_155959"></a><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Customers</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our solutions are deployed in each of the world&#146;s top
20 pharmaceutical companies, in hundreds of large, mid-tier, and emerging
manufacturers, and in 59 countries around the globe.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Approximately 24% and 10%
of our total revenues in 2005 came from our two largest customers, Pfizer and
Sanofi-Aventis, respectively. Approximately 28% and 36% of our total revenues
in 2004 and 2003, respectively, came from our largest client, Pfizer.</font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><a name="Competition_155959"></a><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Competition</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our solutions compete with others principally on the
basis of industry applicability and product flexibility. They also compete on
the basis of name recognition, global competence, service standards, cost,
breadth of customer base and technical support and service. We believe that our
solutions compete favorably with respect to these factors and that we are
positioned to maintain strong market leadership through innovative new product
and application developments and continued focus on support services.</font></p>

<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">

<div>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">While we face a number of
significant competitors in each of our specific market areas, we believe that
there is no single competitor that currently offers our breadth of solutions in
the pharmaceutical and life sciences industries on a worldwide basis. We expect
competition to increase as new competitors enter our markets and as existing
competitors expand their product lines, consolidate or offer more compelling
solutions. We believe that we have distinguished ourselves and are well
positioned in the pharmaceutical market due to our combination of deep
pharmaceutical business knowledge, recognized technical support, depth of
personnel experienced in the pharmaceutical industry and the quality of our
proprietary products and product architecture which is uniquely suited to the
pharmaceutical industry. In addition, we face competition from current
customers and potential customers who may elect to design and install or
operate their own systems.</font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><a name="ResearchAndDevelopment_140836"></a><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Research and Development</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We continue to take advantage of new technologies in
developing new products and services. We work closely with our customers to
develop new products designed directly for their business needs. We recorded
approximately $6,094,000, $9,316,000, and $11,633,000 of research and
development expense for the years ended December&nbsp;31, 2005, 2004 and 2003,
respectively. Our research and development expense plus additions to
capitalized software development costs, was approximately $10,958,000,
$15,202,000 and $14,815,000 for the years ended December&nbsp;31, 2005, 2004
and 2003, respectively. We capitalized less costs in the year ended December&nbsp;31,
2005 than in 2004 due to the development for the release of our next generation
SFE solution, released in 2005.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Dendrite has capitalized
certain costs related to the development of new software products and the
enhancement of existing software products consistent with Statement of
Financial Accounting Standards No.&nbsp;86, &#147;Accounting for the Costs of
Computer Software to be Sold, Leased or Otherwise Marketed.&#148; Capitalized
software development costs net of accumulated amortization were $10,341,000 and
$9,170,000 at December&nbsp;31, 2005 and 2004, respectively.</font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><a name="Seasonality_140837"></a><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Seasonality</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Historically, we have
experienced lower spending from our customers in the first and third quarters
as compared to other quarters. Due to the recent growth of our international
operations, we have been further impacted by lower third quarter spending by
our customers outside the United States.</font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><a name="ProprietaryRights_140837"></a><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Proprietary Rights</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Dendrite relies on
a combination of methods to protect our proprietary rights, including:</font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>trade
secret, copyright and trademark laws;</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>non-disclosure
and other restrictive covenants with our customers, vendors and strategic
partners; and</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>non-disclosure
and other restrictive covenants with our executive officers and other key and
technical employees and consultants.</p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Existing U.S. trade secret
and copyright and trademark laws provide only limited protection for our
proprietary rights, and even less protection may be available under foreign
laws.</font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><a name="Employees_140837"></a><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Employees</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As of December&nbsp;31,
2005, the Company employed 2,793 employees: 1,456 in the U.S. and Canada; 858
in Europe; 279 in the Pacific Rim; and 200 in Latin America.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font style="font-weight:bold;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">John
E. Bailye</font></b></font>&nbsp;&nbsp; has served as Chief Executive Officer
and Director since the Company&#146;s founding in 1987 and since 1991 in the
additional position of Chairman of the Board. Prior to 1987, Mr.&nbsp;Bailye served
as Managing Director of Foresearch Pty., Limited (&#147;Foresearch&#148;), a consulting
company to the pharmaceutical industry in Australia. Mr.&nbsp;Bailye served in
that capacity from the time he acquired Foresearch in 1976 until he sold the
company in 1986. Mr.&nbsp;Bailye served as a market researcher for Foresearch
prior to 1976. Mr.&nbsp;Bailye holds a Bachelors of Commerce in Finance,
Marketing and Business from the University of New South Wales.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font style="font-weight:bold;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Joseph
Ripp</font></b></font><font style="letter-spacing:-.1pt;">&nbsp;&nbsp; </font>has&nbsp;served
as&nbsp;President and Chief Operating Officer since&nbsp;November&nbsp;2005. Prior
to joining the Company, Mr.&nbsp;Ripp held several senior positions within Time
Warner,&nbsp;Inc., most recently serving as Senior Vice President of the Media&nbsp;&amp;
Communications Group.&nbsp;Prior to that position, Mr.&nbsp;Ripp&nbsp;served as
Vice Chairman of America Online,&nbsp;Inc. from 2002 to 2004. Mr.&nbsp;Ripp
also served as Chief Financial Officer of America Online,&nbsp;Inc.; Executive
Vice President and Chief Financial Officer of Time Warner,&nbsp;Inc.; and
Executive Vice President, Chief Financial Officer of Time,&nbsp;Inc. Mr.&nbsp;Ripp
is on the Board of Directors of Greenfield Online,&nbsp;Inc. He is on the Board
of Trustees at Manhattan College, the Board of Directors of the Advertising
Educational Foundation and the Finance Committee of A Better Chance. He also
serves on the Board of Directors and Executive Committee of the Ad Council and
is Chairman of its Finance Committee. Mr.&nbsp;Ripp holds a Bachelor of Arts
degree from Manhattan College and Master of Business Administration from the
Bernard M. Baruch College of the City University of New York.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font style="font-weight:bold;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Jeffrey
J. Bairstow</font></b></font><font style="letter-spacing:-.1pt;">&nbsp;&nbsp; </font>has&nbsp;served
as&nbsp;Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer&nbsp;since&nbsp;December&nbsp;2005.&nbsp;Prior
to joining Dendrite, Mr.&nbsp;Bairstow served as&nbsp;Chief Operating Officer
of RelayHealth Corporation from 2004 to 2005 and Senior Vice President and
Chief Financial Officer of Vitria Technology,&nbsp;Inc. from 2003 to 2004. From
1997 to 2002, Mr.&nbsp;Bairstow held senior management positions within Health
Net,&nbsp;Inc. including Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer
of Health Net-California and President of Health Net&#146;s Government and Specialty
Services Division. Mr.&nbsp;Bairstow has also previously served as&nbsp;Chief
Operating Officer of America Service Group;&nbsp;President of Managed Health
Network, a subsidiary of Health Net,&nbsp;Inc.;&nbsp;Chief Financial Officer
and then President of Vendell Healthcare; and Vice President of Finance and
Corporate Controller and then Chief Operating Officer of </p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font style="font-weight:bold;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Mark
H. Cieplik</font></b></font>&nbsp;&nbsp; has served as Senior Vice President
responsible for the Company&#146;s operations and sales efforts for a major customer
since 2002 and, additionally, for clinical services since 2003. Mr.&nbsp;Cieplik
has been with Dendrite since 1997, previously serving in key senior positions
including Senior Vice President, Worldwide Sales. Prior to joining the Company,
Mr.&nbsp;Cieplik served as Vice President of Americas of Interleaf,&nbsp;Inc.
from 1995 to 1997 and Director of North America Major Accounts for System
Software Associates from 1991 to 1995. Mr.&nbsp;Cieplik also served in various
capacities with IBM from 1976 until 1991. Mr.&nbsp;Cieplik holds a Bachelors of
Science in Marketing from Millikin University.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font style="font-weight:bold;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Natasha
Giordano</font></b></font>&nbsp;&nbsp; has served as Senior Vice President
responsible for global pharmaceutical company sales and Latin American sales
since January&nbsp;2005. Ms.&nbsp;Giordano has been with Dendrite since 2001
and has previously served as Group President, Global Business Unit for major
customers, and Vice President, Global Accounts. Prior to joining Dendrite, Ms.&nbsp;Giordano
spent 10&nbsp;years at Parke-Davis/Warner Lambert in various sales and
sales leadership positions, most recently managing Strategic Alliances. Ms.&nbsp;Giordano
holds a Bachelors of Science degree from Wagner College in New York.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font style="font-weight:bold;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Garry
D. Johnson</font></b></font>&nbsp;&nbsp; has served as Senior Vice President
and Chief Technology Officer since 2003. Mr.&nbsp;Johnson has been with
Dendrite since 2000 and has served as Vice President of North American
Technical Operations. Prior to joining the Company, Mr.&nbsp;Johnson served as
Vice President of Information Technology at Boron Lepore and, prior to that, as
Director, IT Strategy&nbsp;&amp; Quality, at Allied Signal. Mr.&nbsp;Johnson
holds a Bachelors of Arts in Management from Fairfield University.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font style="font-weight:bold;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Jean-Paul
Modde</font></b></font>&nbsp;&nbsp; has served as Senior Vice President responsible
for European and Asia/Pacific sales and marketing and operations since 2003. Mr.&nbsp;Modde
has been with Dendrite since 1988, previously serving in other key management
positions including: Senior Vice President, Asia/Pacific and Latin American
region; Regional Director, Latin America; and Sales Director, Europe. Mr.&nbsp;Modde
holds a Bachelors of Science in Computer Science from Macquarie University,

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font style="font-weight:bold;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Mark Theilken</font></b></font>&nbsp;&nbsp; has
served as Senior Vice President responsible for North American sales, marketing
services, and BuzzeoPDMA sales and operations since January&nbsp;2005. Mr.&nbsp;Theilken
has been with Dendrite since April&nbsp;2004 and has previously served as
Senior Vice President responsible for integrated marketing, data management and
Dendrite&#146;s CRM Effectiveness unit. Prior to joining Dendrite, Mr.&nbsp;Theilken
served as President and Chief Executive Officer of Fuego,&nbsp;Inc. from March&nbsp;2000
to January&nbsp;2004. Prior to Fuego Mr.&nbsp;Theilken spent 5&nbsp;years at
Acxiom Corporation serving as Group Leader, InfoBase Products, and Senior Vice
President, marketing information services. Prior to Acxiom, Mr.&nbsp;Theilken
spent 22&nbsp;years at IBM Corporation. Mr.&nbsp;Theilken holds a Bachelors of
Science in Mathematics from the University of Illinois.</p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 47.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-47.0pt;"><a name="Item2_Properties_140840"></a><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">ITEM 2. Properties</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We lease the following facilities in the U.S.: a
233,000 square foot facility in Bedminster, New Jersey, which serves as our
corporate headquarters; a 137,000 square foot facility in Totowa, New Jersey,
which serves as a distribution center, warehouse and call center for our
integrated marketing business; a 100,000 square foot facility in Chesapeake,
Virginia, which houses a data and call center; a 57,000 square foot facility in
Norcross, Georgia, which serves as a data and call center and hardware repair
and maintenance facility; a 6,700 square foot office in Durham, North Carolina,
which houses certain employees and operations in our data and analytics
business; a 14,000 square foot facility in Woburn Massachusetts which houses
employees and operations for our Optas Division; and a 4,200 square foot office
in Fort Mitchell, Kentucky, a 2,100 square foot office in Mount Laurel, New
Jersey, and a 300 square foot office in San Juan, Puerto Rico each of which
house employees and operations for our BuzzeoPDMA Division. The Bedminster
facility is subleased from Pharmacia&nbsp;&amp; Upjohn Company, a subsidiary of
Pfizer,&nbsp;Inc.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We also lease, or have leased on our behalf, a total
of approximately 378,000 square feet for local management, sales offices and
operations in the following countries: Australia, Austria, Belgium, Brazil,
Canada, China, Colombia, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, India, Italy, Japan,
Mexico, New Zealand, Poland, Portugal, Russia, South Korea, Spain, The
Netherlands, and the United Kingdom.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company also owns a
145,000 square foot facility in Piscataway, New Jersey, which serves as a
hardware repair and maintenance facility; and a 2,500 square foot facility in
Leicestershire, United Kingdom, which is utilized for administrative offices
and integrated marketing operations.</font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 47.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-47.0pt;"><a name="Item3_LegalProceedings_140840"></a><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">ITEM 3. Legal Proceedings</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Dendrite is from time-to-time
involved in litigation relating to personnel and other claims arising in the
ordinary course of business. The Company is not currently engaged in any legal
proceedings that are expected, individually or in the aggregate, to have a
material adverse effect on our business.</font></p>

<p style="line-height:1.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="1" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Approximate Number
of Equity Security Holders</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As of March&nbsp;6, 2006, there were approximately 310
holders of record of our common stock.</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Dividends</font></i></p>

<p style="line-height:11.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company has never paid cash dividends on its
common stock and does not intend to pay cash dividends on common stock in the
foreseeable future. If the Company were to consider paying cash dividends,
certain of the covenants of the Company&#146;s line of credit may limit the amount
of any such dividends we may pay. See Note&nbsp;7 of the Notes to Consolidated
Financial Statements and &#147;Liquidity and Capital Resources&#148; in Item 7 for a
discussion of our credit agreement.</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Issuer Purchases</font></i></p>

<p style="line-height:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 4.0pt 20.0pt;text-indent:-20.0pt;"><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:9.0pt;">(1)</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="1" style="font-size:9.0pt;">Represents shares tendered under the Company&#146;s
replacement option program under which a designated executive may tender shares
of the Company&#146;s common stock owned by the executive in order to pay the
exercise price of vested options and applicable withholdings. The designated
executive receives replacement options in an amount equal to the number of
shares tendered. Each replacement option expires on the expiration date of the
original exercised option to which it relates and the exercised options must be
held for a period of at least one year or the replacement options are
forfeited.</font></p>

<p style="line-height:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 20.0pt;text-indent:-20.0pt;"><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:9.0pt;">(2)</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="1" style="font-size:9.0pt;">Represents shares tendered by an executive
to pay the exercise price of vested options and applicable withholdings in a
transaction under the Company&#146;s 2005 Stock Ownership Incentive Plan.</font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><a name="Item7_ManagementsDiscussionAndAna_164210"></a><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">ITEM 7. Management&#146;s Discussion and Analysis of
Financial Condition and Results of Operations</font></b></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:center;"><a name="InThousands_101700"></a><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">($ in thousands)</font></b></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><a name="ForwardlookingStatements_164210"></a><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Forward-Looking Statements</font></b></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><a name="ExecutiveOverview_164210"></a><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">EXECUTIVE OVERVIEW</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We provide a broad array of solutions worldwide that
enable pharmaceutical and other life science companies to strategically
optimize their sales and marketing channels and clinical resources. Our plan is
to continue to diversify and expand our solutions portfolio, customer base and
geographic reach by leveraging our extensive knowledge of the pharmaceutical
and life sciences industries and capitalizing upon our deep relationships in these
industries. Our strategy continues to rely on both internal growth and
acquisitions to meet to our growth objectives.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We have expanded both our portfolio of solutions and
customer base and believe that this combination presents significant
opportunity for future growth. In January&nbsp;and September&nbsp;2005, we
broadened and enhanced our service portfolio with our acquisitions of
BuzzeoPDMA,&nbsp;Inc. (&#147;Buzzeo&#148;) and Optas,&nbsp;Inc. (&#147;Optas&#148;), respectively.
The Buzzeo acquisition expands our sample and compliance management solution
offerings. The Optas acquisition enhances our portfolio of marketing solutions
services by expanding our privacy-safe relationship marketing solutions for
patients and physicians. We believe our recent acquisitions complement our
existing business operations by enhancing our solutions portfolio, increasing
our access to new customers and allowing deeper penetration into our current
markets. We have also committed to investing in key initiatives to help drive
future growth. Our future growth is dependent on our ability to further
penetrate the markets in which we operate and increase the adoption rate of our
expanded portfolio of solutions.</font></p>


 <p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:24.0pt 0pt .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font face="Times New Roman">16</font></p> <br><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="center">

<!-- SEQ.=1,FOLIO='16',FILE='C:\fc\75101720163_D11241_931147\2977-1-ci.htm',USER='jmsproofassembler',CD='Mar 16 10:17 2006' -->
<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">


<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><font style="font-size:10.0pt;">ITEM 7. Management&#146;s
Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations</font>
(Continued)</font></b></p>

<p style="line-height:11.5pt;margin:0pt 0pt 3.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We evaluate our performance based upon a number of
operating metrics. Chief among these metrics are revenues, operating profit,
diluted net income per share, operating cash flow and days sales outstanding. Our
goal is to execute our strategy to yield growth in revenues, operating profit
and diluted net income per share. In 2005, we grew our revenue approximately
10% but did not grow our operating profit and diluted net income per share. As we
have experienced strong revenue growth in recent years, we believe that we have
outgrown our structure and have seen an increase in organizational costs
throughout 2005. Late in 2005 we appointed two new executive officers who are
evaluating a business plan to grow revenues and to streamline our cost
structure. As part of our effort to realign the Company to drive efficiency and
support our growth objectives, we currently plan to identify approximately $20
million of annualized cost savings during 2006. As a result, we expect to incur
severance and other associated costs for these actions in 2006. We do not
expect to fully realize the savings from these efforts in 2006.</font></p>

<p style="line-height:11.5pt;margin:0pt 0pt 3.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In 2004, we expanded our revenue categories into sales
solutions, marketing solutions and shipping. These categories reflect how our
service offerings have been marketed to and viewed by our customers. They are
not reflective of the way we manage our business. Our operating costs are not
broken out for these categories on a global basis, as they are not viewed as
necessary in the management of our global business. Based upon all of these
factors, while these categories are useful in understanding our operating
results, we have one reporting segment for disclosure purposes under Statement
of Financial Accounting Standards (&#147;SFAS&#148;) 131, &#147;Disclosure About Segments of
an Enterprise and Related Information.&#148; The following is a summary of our
revenue categories:</font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;line-height:11.5pt;margin:0pt 0pt 3.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font style="font-style:italic;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Sales Solutions</font></i></font> revenue
includes products and services of the traditional Dendrite business. All of
these solutions and services are used by or provided to the sales force of our
customers and sales management.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;line-height:11.5pt;margin:0pt 0pt 3.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font style="font-style:italic;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Marketing Solutions </font></i></font>revenue
includes our product and service offerings that are not geared toward the
client sales force and primarily consists of offerings acquired in our business
combinations over the past few years. The primary components of marketing
revenue include integrated marketing, data, consulting and clinical services.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;line-height:11.5pt;margin:0pt 0pt 3.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font style="font-style:italic;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Shipping</font></i></font> revenues are
disclosed separately as they are pass-through costs that bear little to no
margin, and are required to be included in revenues and costs based upon
Emerging Issues Task Force (&#147;EITF&#148;) 00-10, &#147;Accounting for Shipping and
Handling Fees and Costs.&#148; These billable shipping transactions are primarily
related to our integrated marketing activities.</p>

<p style="line-height:11.5pt;margin:0pt 0pt 11.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Management&#146;s Discussion and Analysis (&#147;MD&amp;A&#148;) is
intended to help the reader understand the results of our operations and
financial condition. MD&amp;A is provided as a supplement to, and should be
read in conjunction with our financial statements and the accompanying notes to
consolidated financial statements. Enterprise-wide disclosure information
appearing in Note&nbsp;13 of the Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements are
presented in accordance with SFAS&nbsp;131, &#147;Disclosures about Segments of an
Enterprise and Related Information.&#148;</font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><a name="CriticalAccountingPoliciesJudgmen_164212"></a><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">CRITICAL
ACCOUNTING POLICIES, JUDGMENTS AND ESTIMATES</font></b></p>

<p style="line-height:11.5pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">A
critical accounting policy is one that is both very important to the portrayal
of a company&#146;s financial position and results of operations and requires
management&#146;s most difficult, subjective or complex judgments. We believe that
our critical accounting policies are revenue recognition, acquisitions and
related accruals, impairments, income taxes and capitalized software.</font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><a name="RevenueRecognition_164212"></a><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Revenue Recognition</font></b></p>

<p style="line-height:11.5pt;margin:0pt 0pt 4.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The area of revenue recognition requires management&#146;s
to make significant judgments and estimates. AICPA Statement of Position (&#147;SOP&#148;)
97-2, &#147;Software Revenue Recognition,&#148; governs revenue recognition for
arrangements that include software which is more than incidental to the
arrangement. Under SOP 97-2, if a sale of software includes services that
are essential to the functionality of the</font></p>


 <p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:24.0pt 0pt .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font face="Times New Roman">17</font></p> <br><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="center">

<!-- SEQ.=1,FOLIO='17',FILE='C:\fc\75101720163_D11241_931147\2977-1-ci.htm',USER='jmsproofassembler',CD='Mar 16 10:17 2006' -->
<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">


<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">ITEM 7. Management&#146;s
Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations (Continued)</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">software, then the software and essential services are
to be accounted for using contract accounting as described in Accounting
Research Bulletin 45, &#147;Long-Term Construction-Type Contracts,&#148; and SOP 81-1,
&#147;Accounting for Performance of Construction-Type and Certain Production-Type
Contracts.&#148; The determination of whether or not services are essential to the
functionality of the software can differ from arrangement-to-arrangement
and requires the use of significant judgment by management. Factors used in
determining whether or not services are essential to the functionality may
include: whether or not physical changes are being made to the software&#146;s
underlying source code; the complexity of software configuration services; the
level of effort required to build interfaces; the overall relationship of the
service fees to the license fees; the length of time expected to complete the
services; and whether or not the services can be obtained by a customer from
their internal resources or another third-party vendor. If services are
not considered to be essential to the functionality of the software, SOP 97-2
generally allows companies to recognize revenue for software licenses upon
delivery of the licenses, prior to configuration or implementation services,
provided that the other requirements of the SOP are met. In management&#146;s
judgment, our configuration and implementation services generally are essential
to the functionality of our software. Therefore, we typically recognize revenue
using the percentage-of-completion method as detailed in SOP 81-1.</font></p>

<p style="line-height:11.5pt;margin:0pt 0pt 4.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The percentage-of-completion method of revenue
recognition requires us to use significant estimates in measuring the
progress-to-completion for each project. For our license fee and implementation
service projects, we use the input measure of labor incurred as compared with
total expected labor for the entire project. The determination of total project
labor requires the use of significant judgment and estimates. We review these
estimates on a monthly basis. Actual results could differ from these estimates,
which would impact the amount of revenue previously recognized, had better
estimates been available at the time.</font></p>

<p style="line-height:11.5pt;margin:0pt 0pt 4.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Many of our arrangements include multiple
deliverables. In the absence of higher-level specific authoritative
guidance, we determine the units of accounting for multiple element
arrangements in accordance with Emerging Issues Task Force Issue No.&nbsp;00-21,
&#147;Revenue Arrangements with Multiple Deliverables&#148; (&#147;EITF 00-21&#148;).
Specifically, we will consider a delivered item as a separate unit of
accounting if it has value to the customer on a stand-alone basis, if
there is objective and reliable evidence of the fair value of the undelivered
elements, and if the arrangement includes a general right of return relative to
the delivered element, delivery or performance of the undelivered element is
considered probable and is substantially within our control. The determination
of whether or not arrangements meet these criteria requires significant
judgment on the part of the management. If our arrangements did not meet the
separation criteria of EITF 00-21, the timing of revenue recognition
could be delayed.</font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><a name="AccountingForAcquisitions_164213"></a><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Accounting for Acquisitions</font></b></p>

<p style="line-height:11.5pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The
accounting related to business combinations requires us to estimate the fair
value and useful life of the assets acquired and the fair value of the
liabilities assumed in the combinations. These estimates of fair value are
based on our business plan for the entities acquired including planned redundancies,
restructuring, use of assets acquired and assumptions as to the ultimate
resolution of obligations assumed for which no future benefit will be received.
We typically analyze a number of factors such as valuation or appraisal reports
when determining the estimates of fair value. Should actual use of assets or
resolution of obligations differ from our estimates, revisions to the estimated
fair values, useful lives, or both, would be required.</font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><a name="AccountingForImpairments_164214"></a><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Accounting for Impairments</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We review long-lived assets for impairment on an
annual basis or whenever events or changes in circumstances indicate that the
carrying amount of an asset might not be recoverable. Other than goodwill </font></p>


 <p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:24.0pt 0pt .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font face="Times New Roman">18</font></p> <br><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="center">

<!-- SEQ.=1,FOLIO='18',FILE='C:\fc\75101720163_D11241_931147\2977-1-ci.htm',USER='jmsproofassembler',CD='Mar 16 10:17 2006' -->
<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">


<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">ITEM 7. Management&#146;s
Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations (Continued)</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">and indefinite-lived intangibles, if indicators
of impairment are present, we evaluate the recoverability of the long-lived
assets by estimating future undiscounted cash flows that are directly
associated with and expected to arise as a direct result of the use and
eventual disposition of the long-lived asset. If this estimate of future
undiscounted cash flows demonstrates that recoverability is not probable, an
impairment loss would be calculated and recognized based on the excess carrying
value of the long-lived asset over the long-lived asset&#146;s fair value. The
estimate of the fair value and the future undiscounted cash flows of the
underlying long-lived assets are based on significant judgments and
assumptions.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We review capitalized software development costs and
purchased capitalized software development costs for impairment at each balance
sheet date to determine if the unamortized capitalized costs of a computer
software product is greater than the net realizable value of that product. In
instances where the unamortized capitalized costs are greater than the net
realizable value, we would record an impairment loss.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We assess goodwill
and indefinite-lived intangibles for the possibility of impairment on an
annual basis (as of October&nbsp;1 of each year), and whenever events or
changes in circumstances indicate that the carrying values may not be
recoverable. Some factors we consider important which could trigger an
impairment review include the following:</font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Significant
underperformance relative to historical or projected future operating results;</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Significant
changes in our use of acquired assets or the strategy for our overall business;
and</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Significant
negative industry or economic trends.</p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On an annual basis, or when we determine that the
carrying value of goodwill may not be recoverable based upon the existence of
one or more of the above indicators of impairment, we calculate and compare the
fair value of our reporting unit to its carrying value. We currently have only
one reporting unit. If the carrying value exceeds the fair value, we calculate
the implied fair value of the goodwill for our reporting unit and compare it to
the carrying value of the goodwill. If the implied fair value of the goodwill
was less than the carrying value of the goodwill, we would recognize an
impairment loss, (not to exceed the carrying value) in our consolidated
statement of operations.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On an annual basis, or
when we determine that the carrying value of an indefinite-lived
intangible asset may not be recoverable based upon the existence of one or more
of the above indicators of impairment, we calculate and compare the fair value
of the indefinite-lived intangible asset to its carrying value. If the
carrying value exceeds the fair value, an impairment loss would be recognized.
If we deem the useful life to be no longer indefinite, after testing for
impairment in accordance with the applicable rules&nbsp;stated above, we
amortize the intangible asset over its remaining estimated useful life,
following the pattern in which the expected benefits will be consumed or
otherwise used up and we would continue to review for impairment in the future
on an annual basis.</font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><a name="AccountingForIncomeTaxes_164215"></a><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Accounting for Income Taxes</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Deferred tax assets and
liabilities represent the differences between the financial reporting and tax
basis of assets and liabilities and are measured using the enacted tax rates
that are expected to be in effect when the differences reverse. We regularly
review our deferred tax assets for recoverability and establish a valuation
allowance based on historical taxable income, projected future taxable income
and the expected timing of the reversals of existing temporary differences, all
of which require significant judgment. We must believe it is more likely than
not that the recorded net deferred tax asset will be realized. Realization is
dependent on generating sufficient taxable income of a specific nature prior to
the expiration of the loss </font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">carryforwards, capital loss and foreign tax credit
carryforwards. The asset may be reduced if estimates of future taxable income
during the carryforward period are reduced. In addition, we maintain reserves
